reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that p–d orbital hybridization in a different Pt-based HEA (PtRuNiCoFeGaPbW) suppresses CO intermediate adsorption and improves methanol oxidation selectivity, but it does not address thermal annealing, atomic reordering, or ethanol oxidation on PtPdRhRuIrOs. The key premises about annealing-induced reordering, its effect on p–d hybridization, and the specific poisoning intermediates in ethanol oxidation are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Thermal annealing of PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts induces atomic reordering without phase segregation
Atomic reordering enhances p–d orbital hybridization between Pt and neighbouring atoms
Enhanced p–d orbital hybridization shifts the Pt d-band center
A shifted Pt d-band center weakens adsorption of poisoning intermediates during ethanol oxidation
Weakened poisoning intermediate adsorption improves selectivity and durability
